notes: Introspects a live JDBC-connected database and generates a browsable HTML ERD site. Read-only/generator pattern, not an editor — 'CRUD' here means changing the underlying DB, then regenerating. Solid fit for 'document what Fivetran landed', weak fit for iterative wireframing.

package: PlantUML (+ plantuml-generator / genuml for Java source)
notes: Text-first (.puml), so it diffs cleanly and an agent can CRUD the diagram source directly — best versioning story in the Java column. Default rendering is the weakest-looking of the shortlisted tools; needs a theme/skinparam pass to look presentable to a non-engineer audience.
Explicitly deprecated per JHipster's own docs — included only to record that it was checked and ruled out, not as a live candidate.

package: mermaid erDiagram (via any JVM HTTP call to mmdc, or a JVM Graal/JS embed)
notes: No native JVM Mermaid renderer exists; a Java service would shell out to the Node-based mmdc CLI or call a rendering microservice. Listed because it's realistically the best-looking, best-versioned option available to a JVM shop, at the cost of a cross-runtime dependency.

Actively maintained (last update 2026-05-10). Introspects any JDBC-reachable database and outputs DOT, PlantUML, or dbdiagram.io (DBML) format directly, plus HTML5-with-embedded-diagrams reports — the widest output-format spread of any Java tool reviewed, and the only one that targets a modern text-diagram format (DBML/PlantUML) instead of just Graphviz.
